Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Pacifica Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Jennifer Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Pacifica Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are David Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Laura Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Chris Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Emily Wong, Chief Strategy Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; and Karen Brooks, Chief Regulatory Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Harlan.

David Harlan: Thank you, Jennifer, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Effective management of regulatory lag and proactive mitigation strategies.
    2. Strong results compared to prior periods and progress toward guidance.
    3. Robust rate base growth outlook and supporting assumptions.
    4. Disciplined capital expenditure plan and key project advancements.
    5. Superior reliability metrics including SAIDI and SAIFI, alongside overall system performance.
    6. Targeted O&M expense management initiatives yielding meaningful efficiency gains.
    7. Constructive dialogue with analysts on critical topics shaping our outlook.

These elements highlight our resilience across regulated utilities, competitive generation, and renewables amid inflation, weather volatility, and the clean energy transition. Now, I'll turn the call over to Laura Chen to discuss the financials in greater detail.

Laura Chen: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.92 and revenue of $2.48 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's still morning here on the West Coast. Thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call for Pacifica Energy Corp. As your CFO, I'll walk you through our financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2024, provide a detailed comparison to the prior-year period and the sequential quarter, and outline our updated guidance. I'll focus on key non-GAAP metrics like adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS, which best reflect our underlying operational performance, excluding one-time items such as mark-to-market hedges and regulatory disallowances.

Starting with the headline numbers: Consolidated revenues reached $2.48 billion, up 7.2% from $2.31 billion in Q3 2023 and up 4.1% sequentially from Q2 2024's $2.38 billion. Adjusted EBITDA was $812 million, a 14.8% increase year-over-year from $707 million and 8.3% higher than Q2's $750 million. Adjusted diluted EPS hit $0.92, up 17.9% from $0.78 in the prior-year quarter and 8.2% above Q2's $0.85. Year-to-date adjusted EPS stands at $2.41, on track for the high end of our full-year outlook.

Breaking it down by segment, our regulated utilities—including transmission and distribution in PJM and MISO across the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic—saw revenues of $1.12 billion, up 6.5% YoY from $1.05 billion, driven by 3.8% retail load growth from data centers and EV infrastructure, plus approved rate cases adding $85 million to rate base. Adjusted EBITDA rose 12.1% to $420 million, with O&M down 5% thanks to digital workforce tools cutting overtime 18%. Margins expanded 150 basis points sequentially to 37.5%.

In competitive generation, anchored by our 1,200 MW Liberty Peaker in ERCOT, revenues grew 9.4% YoY to $950 million on $45/MWh spark spreads amid heat waves and hyperscaler demand. Capacity factor reached 68% from 62%, heat rates improved to 7,200 Btu/kWh, and EBITDA surged 22% to $285 million. Coal-to-gas shifts saved $12 million.

Renewables and storage revenues climbed 12.7% to $450 million, powered by 450 MW SunForge solar in CAISO and 200 MW/800 MWh IronPeak battery in ERCOT, capturing $28 million in ancillaries. Wind capacity factors averaged 38%, solar 26% DC, with EBITDA up 18% to $187 million at 41.6% margins, aided by IRA tax credits.

Key drivers included 4.2% system load growth outpacing EIA averages, stable $2.85/MMBtu gas with 75% hedges, O&M down 7% to $22.50/MWh via PowerOptix digital twins cutting outages 25%, and $650 million capex focused on grid hardening post-Hurricane Idalia. Regulatory lag shaved margins but formula rates recovered $18 million. ERCOT led EBITDA growth at 22%, PJM offset softer spreads with 93% nuclear factors, CAISO buffered by storage.

Balance sheet strong at $4.2 billion liquidity, 3.2x net debt/EBITDA. We're raising full-year 2024 guidance: adjusted EBITDA $3.15-$3.25 billion, up from $3.05-$3.20 billion; adjusted EPS $3.35-$3.45, from $3.20-$3.35, implying 10-12% growth. For 2025, 7-9% EPS growth to $3.60-$3.75, with 6-8% long-term CAGR via 1.2 GW renewables and CCUS retrofits.

Today, I'd also like to dive deeper into regulatory lag—a persistent industry headwind amplified by capex escalation from clean energy, grid hardening, and inflation. For Pacifica Energy Corp., it stems from the mismatch between upfront infrastructure investments and rate recovery. Q2 2024 net lag was $285 million, up 18% YoY from $240 million, compressing regulated EBITDA margins 120 bps to 27.3% from 28.5%.

Our $2.8 billion 2024 capex—55% T&D resilience, 30% renewables/storage, 15% customer programs—outpaced rate base growth by 12%. Inflation added 15-20% to T&D costs, WECC wholesale power up 25% on hydro droughts. In Oregon PUC territory, lag is $150 million due to post-facto wildfire capex reviews ($450 million annual, undergrounding 500 miles, AI vegetation like Xcel). Washington UTC caps at $90 million via multi-year plans, California JVs benefit from risk-of-return but face AB 1054 volatility.

Mitigation is multi-pronged to close lag under $200 million by 2025 end. Rate cases: Q1 Oregon GRC seeks $320 million increase with MYRP to 2027, 60% CWIP unlocking $180 million; Washington ROE ratchets to 10.2%. Trackers cover 70% incremental costs: Wildfire Fund ($100 million securitized), FPP offsetting $75 million hydro, FERC TCAM for transmission, RPS for 800 MW solar/4 GWh BESS with 90/10 PPAs.

PBR pilot in Washington ties 50 bps ROE to reliability, decarbonization (85% carbon-free by 2030, SMRs with NuScale), affordability, DER (2 GW VPPs). Digital twins via GE GridOS optimize $300 million capex 10-15%, hydro forecast 92% accuracy saves $20 million. Self-supply: 1.2 GW renewables backlog at 15% IRR, $400 million wind acquisition at 11x EBITDA.

Lag peaks Q4 at $300 million, down 25% 2025 with $500 million AFUDC. Five-year $14 billion capex drives 6-8% EPS CAGR, ROE to 10.5%.

Turning to rate base growth: Our regulated rate base was $52.4 billion at quarter-end, up 6.8% YoY on $4.2 billion capex in service, earning 10.25% ROE. We guide 6.5-7.0% CAGR to $72 billion by 2028, assuming constructive regulation, capex execution, 1.8-2.2% load growth in six-state Southeast/Midwest footprint.

Annual capex $4.5-$5.0 billion: 60% T&D ($1.2 billion resiliency, undergrounding 1,500 miles, Siemens automation), 25% generation (1.2 GW solar like Oak Grove 400 MW, 500 MW BESS GE GridSolv, $400 million Cumberland CCGT HA turbines with Occidental DAC), 15% customer (5,000 EV chargers, 85% AMI).

Regulatory: 100% CWIP recovery, Georgia $250 million approved, Virginia $180 million, pending NC $320 million; two more cases by 2026 for $400 million. Load: Southeast data centers 3 GW (Meta/Google), Midwest 800 MW industrial, peak to 28,000 MW. Digital synchrophasors cut outages 20%, H2 pilots at nuclear. Funding 60% debt/5.25%, FFO/debt 18%.

Risks: weather, rate delays, supply chains; upsides data centers, IRA ITCs.

On capex plan: Reaffirming 2024 at $2.6 billion, up 8% YoY; 2025-2027 $8.7 billion, 12% CAGR—45% generation, 40% T&D, 15% customer. Generation $1.2 billion: Prairie Winds 800 MW solar+400 MWh LFP storage Illinois MISO ($850 million, $0.85/Wdc, 12% IRR); ERCOT 450 MW/900 MWh batteries Tesla Megapack (92% RTE, Google PPAs $120/MWh); $220 million CCGT H2 retrofits, NuScale SMR Ohio 77 MW by 2029.

T&D $1.0 billion: DLR pilots ABB 345 kV Pennsylvania +20-30% capacity, ERCOT undergrounding Houston, ERCOT 25% of plan. Customer $400 million: 95% AMI, EV with Siemens GridX.

Supports 10.2% ROE, IRA de-risks, A- rating.

Finally, on O&M: 9M 2024 O&M $1.42 billion, down 7.2% YoY ($110 million savings) to 21.1% of revenues. Pillars: predictive maintenance (45% savings, GE Predix/Siemens MindSphere, CCGT sensors cut EFOR 18%, Liberty Creek 2.2% heat rate save $12 million, nuclear drones 25% outages); supply chain (30%, 70% 2025 gas hedged Cheniere, vendor cuts 11%); workforce digitization (15%, SAP S/4HANA 65% automation, contractor down 22%); renewables (10%, drones Siemens wind 41.5% CF, Nextracker solar 8% soiling).

ERCOT offset 22% load growth, PJM nuclear uprates, CAISO BESS duck curve. Target 5-6% cut 2025, ROIC 25%.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $650 million, primarily focused on renewables deployment and grid hardening. We remain committed to a strong balance sheet and shareholder returns, anticipating our raised outlook.

Now, over to Chris for operations.

Chris Patel: Thank you, Laura. Let me provide an update on the operational front. Reliability is foundational at Pacifica Energy Corp., serving 4.2 million customers in the Midwest and Southeast. We rank top quartile in J.D. Power for three years running, aiding rate cases.

Full-year 2023 SAIDI was 112.4 minutes, down 22% from 2022's 145.1, below EIA median 128 and our 120 target. SAIFI 1.05 vs 1.32, under 1.18 benchmark. YTD Q3 2024 annualized SAIDI 78.2 minutes, SAIFI 0.92—best pace ever.

Trends: SAIDI 162.3 (2021), 145.1 (2022), 112.4 (2023), 78.2 (2024 ann.); SAIFI 1.48 to 0.92. Weather drove 42% 2022 interruptions, but investments turned it around. Midwest SAIDI 98.7 (2023) vs 135 (2022), Q2 derechos restored 95% in 4 hours. Southeast 132 minutes impacted by Idalia, but major event days down 28% via coastal undergrounding—better than Duke 145, Southern 138.

CAIDI 107 minutes, MAIFI down 15% to 2.4, 99.96% availability NERC compliant. $1.2 billion 2023 capex (12% total): LiDAR drones 25,000 miles ROW cut tree outages 35% (Trimble AI, FERC 881); 1.8 million AMI (85%), GE ADMS OSIsoft cut detection 45 to 12 minutes; composite poles 850 miles, 200 MW microgrids; StormShield Ohio $250 million PUCO riders targets 20% SAIDI cut.

DER IEEE 1547 tools for 15% rooftop solar. Illinois settlement $150 million multiplier. Guide 2024 SAIDI <100 excluding majors, $1.4 billion capex.

We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas power plants due to digital twin platforms and predictive maintenance. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 22%.

Thank you. Over to Emily.

Emily Wong: Thank you, Chris. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the ERCOT market, targeting assets like wind-plus-storage at attractive 9-11x multiples to support our 60% carbon-free goal by 2030.

Raj?

Raj Singh: Thank you, Emily. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed an advanced cybersecurity solution to enhance our defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting synchrophasor technology in our Oregon service territory, enabling real-time wide-area monitoring and 20% outage reductions per EPRI standards.

Karen?

Karen Brooks: Thank you, Raj. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our general rate case in Oregon. This will allow us to recover $320 million in increased revenues through a multi-year rate plan with substantial CWIP inclusion.

David Harlan: Thank you, Laura, Chris, Emily, Raj, and Karen. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and commitment to long-term shareholder value. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Julien Dumoulin-Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Julien Dumoulin-Smith: Thanks, good morning everyone. Strong beat on adjusted EPS at $0.92 versus our $0.85 estimate, and revenue up 7.2% year-over-year to $2.48 billion. Can you walk us through the drivers there, particularly the outperformance in the unregulated power gen segment, and any color on forward load growth from hyperscalers given the AI boom?

David Harlan: Good morning, Julien. The EPS beat stemmed from regulated ops with 3.8% weather-normalized load growth, 15% commercial ramp—data centers 25% of incrementals in PJM/MISO. Signed three 15-year PPAs with hyperscalers totaling 1.2 GW at $65/MWh blended, 20% above marginal costs. Unregulated gen margins up 250 bps to around 40% on spark spreads, Henry Hub $2.85/MMBtu, gas fleet 68% capacity factor hedged at $2.60. Nuclear 93% across 2.4 GW added $180 million margins. Hyperscalers underpin 40% of 2024-2028 load growth, now 4.5-5.5% CAGR from 3.5-4.5%; RFPs from Microsoft/Google for 800 MW ERCOT.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Arcaro with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Arcaro: Thanks. On capex, you guided $2.6 billion for 2024, midpoint now higher. Breakdown on renewables versus thermal sustainment, and how does this tie into your 7-9% EPS growth in 2025? Also, any updates on SMR deployment timelines?

Laura Chen: David, capex midpoint $2.6 billion, reflecting solar/battery acceleration. Alloc: 55% or ~$1.4 billion renewables—1.5 GW solar-plus-storage CAISO/SPP, 8-10% IRRs ITC-boosted to 12%; 20% grid hardening/EV Northeast; thermal $800 million nuclear uprates (200 MW steam generators), coal-to-CCCT. Supports 7-9% 2025 EPS: regulated 10.2% ROE on growing rate base, unregulated ROIC to 13.5%. SMRs: NuScale advanced talks 462 MW retired site ISO-NE, NRC pre-app done, FID H2 2025, COD 2030, LCOE <$60/MWh.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your reliability metrics this quarter—specifically SAIDI and SAIFI—and how they tie into overall system performance. With the severe weather events we've seen, can you walk us through the year-to-date figures, trends, and any key initiatives driving improvements?

Chris Patel: Great question, Sarah. Reliability underpins everything. 2023 SAIDI 112.4 minutes (down 22%), SAIFI 1.05; YTD 2024 ann. 78.2/0.92. Trends show steady improvement post-weather events. Initiatives: LiDAR drones cut tree outages 35%, ADMS detection to 12 minutes, hardening projects, DER tools. Positions us for ROE upsides.

Operator: Our next question comes from Stephen Byrd with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Stephen Byrd: Morning, team. Balance sheet looks solid—FFO-to-debt at 18% pro forma, net debt-to-EBITDA 3.2x. Dividend implications, and any M&A appetite post recent bolt-ons?

Laura Chen: Morning, Stephen. Fortress balance sheet: $4.2 billion liquidity. FFO/debt 17-19% through 2025. Payout 70% DCF, 5-7% hikes; $1.1 billion buybacks. M&A opportunistic: recent 300 MW wind accretive at 11x; pipeline Midwest batteries, PJM peakers >10% IRR.

Operator: Our next question comes from Noelle Cagle with Stephens. Please go ahead.

Noelle Cagle: Thanks. Regional color: ERCOT drove gen margins, but winter storm risks? Clean energy transition navigation amid PTC/ITC uncertainty and state pushback?

David Harlan: Noelle, ERCOT standout—gas fleet $150/MWh peaks added $120 million EBITDA, batteries flawless ancillaries $25 million, Texas up 22% to $450 million. IRA $1.8 billion credits 90% monetized; Ohio approved 800 MW solar formula recovery. Coal derated to 20%, CCGTs 45%, 60% renewables/nuclear/storage 2030. Hedged 85% gas, pushing FERC 2222.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to David Harlan for closing remarks.

David Harlan: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Pacifica Energy Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Pacifica Energy Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
